query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys by eliminating weak boundaries and inducing a microstructure that prevents premature crack nucleation.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies and numerous internal boundaries
generation.conditions: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructure with a skeletal, non-recrystallized B2 phase and a recrystallized FCC phase
generation.mechanism: PSR eliminates weak boundaries, preventing premature crack nucleation, and allows both phases to contribute to strain hardening simultaneously through high-density dislocation multiplication and a strain-induced B2 to BCT phase transformation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and room-temperature tensile ductility, with a uniform elongation of ~33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ~2.2 GPa
generation.baseline: As-cast or fully recrystallized eutectic high-entropy alloys with limited ductility
generation.boundary: The PSR strategy is effective for eutectic high-entropy alloys with a specific microstructure, and its applicability to other alloy systems needs to be explored
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms of PSR and its effects on the microstructure and mechanical properties of eutectic high-entropy alloys are not fully understood and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature on PSR-processed eutectic high-entropy alloys with varying microstructures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the PSR-processed alloys do not exhibit improved strength and ductility compared to the as-cast or fully recrystallized alloys, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement. Findings: The phase-selectively recrystallized (PSR) EHEA achieves a uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa.; The PSR EHEA exhibits a fracture true strain of ∼30%, which is double that of the As-cast (AC) alloy (∼14%) and the fully recrystallized (FR) alloy (∼17%).; The fracture true stress of the PSR EHEA reaches ∼1850 MPa, significantly higher than the AC (∼1390 MPa) and FR (∼1460 MPa)
